mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: What: A wooden toy with an NFC chip links to a playground discovery PWA. Children check in, earn badges, print them through the company website, color them, glue them into a handmade passport. Every print sends a parent to the product catalog — without an ad, a popup, or a captured email.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Why: Children's apps monetize attention. Growth hacking monetizes trust. Both extract more than they give. Vrooom inverts the model: the utility earns the visit, the visit earns the discovery, the discovery earns the next purchase — if the product deserves it.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: How: NFC as entry point, zero accounts, zero tracking, E2E encrypted WebRTC bridge to website for printing. The product serves an immediate need with no compromise. The business grows because people come back, not because they're brought back.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Proof: 15 seconds of screen time per session. Zero data sent to any server. The growth channel is a parent choosing to print something for their child.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: -- Role: Systems Designer & Product Strategist Key supporter: Thomas Duester — kept pushing when I was ready to move on. Some projects survive because someone else refuses to let them die.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Stack: Vanilla JS, Three.js, Leaflet, Overpass API, Valhalla routing, Dexie.js Design metric: Screen time measured in seconds per interaction, not minutes. A child runs to the bench where her father sits. She holds up a stick — a wand, perhaps, or a sword, or something that has no name yet because she is still deciding. She wants him to see.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: He glances up from his phone. "That's nice, honey." His eyes return to the screen. She waits. The stick lowers. She walks back to the grass, alone. The phone is not the villain. The phone is the symptom. The villain is the exhaustion, the isolation, the impossible demands placed on parents who have no village. The phone fills the vacuum we created.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: But what else could fill it? Children's apps are a billion-dollar industry built on a single transaction: silence purchased with screen time. Engagement is the metric. Retention is the goal. The app succeeds when the child does not look up.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Behind this industry sits another one: growth hacking. Captured emails. Retargeting pixels. Push notifications. Streak mechanics. Dark patterns dressed as engagement. The business model requires the user to be brought back — because the product alone is not worth returning to.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: What if the product was worth returning to? A wooden car. Beech — closed grain, food-safe, built to outlast the child who holds it. Inside: an NFC tag. Tap it to a parent's phone and a PWA opens — a playground discovery app that checks in at parks, earns badges, and gets out of the way. Fifteen seconds of screen time per session. No account. No data sent anywhere. No push notifications. No streaks.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The app serves one need: a child wants to explore. It serves it completely, then disappears. Brands win more from being remembered for what they leave behind than from what they took. The toy does not need the phone. The phone needs the parent. This is the foundation. A product that respects its user has earned something no retargeting pixel can buy: trust. A parent who trusts the product comes back. Not because they were reminded. Because they chose to.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The shape descends from a childhood memory — matchbox cars with cork wheels. Why those toys lasted was not their complexity. It was their simplicity. They were substrates for play, not scripts for it. No doors, no windows, no driver. Every detail removed is a story the child gets to add.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Hand-planed from rectangular blocks — finding the right taper, grip, and weight happened physically, not in CAD. The bottom tapers at front and back — not decoration, but function. Push it like a friction toy and the taper lifts it slightly, prevents scratching, makes the glide smooth. There is a Japanese carpentry principle: build it in a way that it lasts as long as it took the tree to grow.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The first prototypes went to neighborhood kids. No instructions, no explanation. They connected with the object before anyone mentioned the app. The wood, the weight, the shape. If the physical object does not stand alone — if it needs the digital to justify itself — the design has failed. The NFC inside is an expansion, not a requirement.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The design goal for the first moment a child taps the car to a parent's phone: nothing less than magic. Eyes shining. The thing in their hand was hiding this all along.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: A product people love is a product people return to. That is not a marketing insight. It is a design decision. No avatar, no account, no login. The child's identity in the app is their wooden car. The NFC tag carries a URL pointing to a car configuration — a 3D model with mapped parts, colors, and sounds. Tap the car to the phone, and it appears on screen: a rendered wooden toy that spins, responds to touch, and revs its engine. The 3D viewer captures a side-view snapshot that becomes the child's marker on the map. Their car drives across the neighborhood as they walk.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: No "select a playground" step. No trip planning. The child walks. When they arrive — a playground, a park, a pool — they tap "I'm here." Fresh GPS, nearest match within 150 metres, visit logged.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The badge system is designed to end in paper, not pixels. Playground badges — one per unique place visited Regular badges — earned after 10 visits to the same place Milestone badges — shields for 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 unique playgrounds

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: All badges are SVG line art. Intentionally uncolored. The badge page connects to the Vrooom website via end-to-end encrypted WebRTC — a single button, no account, no cloud. The 3D car viewer doubles as a coloring-book generator — choose an angle and it renders a line-art outline ready for printing.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Print the badges. Cut along the lines. Color them in. Color the car. Glue them into a handmade passport. The badges end in paper. But the path to paper passes through the Vrooom website. That visit is not accidental. A parent standing at a printer, waiting for badge sheets, is standing inside the company's product catalog. No banner. No popup. No "you might also like." They came because the app was useful. They stay because the products are visible. They return because their child earned new badges.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: This is led-growth without the growth hacking. No captured email. No retargeting pixel. No notification asking them to come back. The utility earns the visit. The visit earns the discovery. The discovery earns the next purchase — if the product deserves it.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Every children's app monetizes attention. Vrooom monetizes the moment a parent chooses to print something for their child. The difference is who holds the power in that transaction.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Gamification. No points, no streaks, no leaderboards. The moment you add streaks, you add anxiety. A playground is not a competition.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Social features. No friends, no sharing, no "see where other kids are." Social features shift focus from exploration to performance. The child should discover playgrounds because they are curious, not because their friend did.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Turn-by-turn navigation. Vrooom shows walking routes when asked, but does not guide. A child walking to a playground should look at the world, not at a screen.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Photo capture. Rejected — it puts the phone back in the child's hands at the moment they should be playing. The check-in is the record. The badge is the memory.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Child-held device. The phone belongs to the parent. If the child holds the phone, the phone becomes the toy. If the parent holds the phone, the phone becomes the bridge.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: Ads, emails, push notifications. The conventional growth toolkit. Every one of them trades user trust for a short-term metric. The product grows by being worth returning to, or it does not grow.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: A shape that carries no date cannot become dated. A material that ages cannot become obsolete. Fifty years from now, the same car will feel the same in a child's hand, will invite the same open stories, will wait for the same imagination to bring it alive.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: And perhaps, by then, it will carry something more. The passport stamps from trips that became legends. The layers of memory pressed into an object, invisible as the NFC chip, present as the wood's weight.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The toy is not the legacy. The play is the legacy. The toy is just what holds it. Vrooom is the third project in the physical-digital-bridge cluster: Drop — bottle cap triggers water map. Utility. Pebbble — stone triggers encrypted voice. Presence. Vrooom — wooden car triggers playground discovery. Play.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: But Vrooom adds something the others don't: the output is physical too. The digital layer is sandwiched between two physical ones — a wooden car on one end, a paper passport on the other.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: And Vrooom carries a question the others don't ask. Drop proves that public infrastructure can replace proprietary APIs. Pebbble proves that privacy can be enforced by architecture. Vrooom demonstrates something else: a working system where the business model and the user's interest are structurally aligned — not by policy, not by promise, but by architecture. The parent goes to the website because they want to, not because they were nudged.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: The companies that need this thinking are the ones starting to realize that the extraction model has a ceiling. Users leave. Regulation tightens. Brand trust erodes. The ones who figure out how to grow by giving more than they take will outlast the ones still optimizing click-through rates.

mine.title: Vrooom
mine.text: A car in the hand. A playground around the corner. The phone already forgotten.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Creator — Systems Designer & Design Engineer — 2026 — solo Why: Every Record of Processing Activities tool on the market turns a spatial, relational question — how does personal data move through our organisation?

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: — into a spreadsheet. The structure of the tool prevents the understanding it is supposed to produce.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: What: A local-first workbench where hand-drawn shapes become GDPR compliance modules, connected by Sankey-style bands whose thickness shows how much personal data flows through and whose colour shows how exposed it is.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A canvas that recognises drawings on the device. A scoring formula published openly so anyone can inspect it.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Zero server infrastructure.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Outcome: The tool that maps an organisation's data flows never lets that map leave the device.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The scoring is published mathematics, not vendor opinion. The act of building the flow teaches the regulation's logic — the interaction IS the audit.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: AutoFlow is an independent project — a data sovereignty workbench for domain experts who bear legal responsibility for personal data they cannot technically protect.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: HR managers, GPs, compliance officers, legal secretaries: people told to "anonymise this before sharing it" without ever being given a tool that lets them do so without involving a developer or a cloud service.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Built solo, in vanilla web components, with on-device classification and a published scoring model.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: GDPR requires every organisation processing personal data to maintain a Record of Processing Activities — Article 30.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The industry response was spreadsheets, SaaS dashboards, and compliance platforms that turn a regulation about protecting people into a data entry exercise.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A Data Protection Officer opens a tool, fills in fields, saves a row.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The output is a table that satisfies an auditor but teaches no one anything about where risk actually lives.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The problem is not that these tools are bad at their job. The problem is that their job is wrong.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A ROPA describes a network — who collects personal data, what happens to it, where it is stored, who receives it.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: That is a spatial, directional, relational question. Every tool on the market answers it with rows and columns.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: When a DPO needs to know "what happens to health records after they enter our system?

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: " — the answer is a path through a network. Not cell B247.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: There is a second problem layered on the first. The data a DPO enters into a ROPA tool is itself sensitive — a complete map of an organisation's personal data processing.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The market leaders host that map on third-party servers, often under US jurisdiction.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The compliance tool creates a compliance problem about the compliance tool.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The territory and the map should be made from the same material.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The first sketches were node graphs. Boxes, lines, arrows — the obvious answer when you say "diagram.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: " They failed almost immediately. A node graph lets you connect anything to anything, which is technically expressive and operationally meaningless.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A DPO does not need infinite freedom. They need a sequence — where the data enters, what happens to it, where it leaves.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Freedom was making the structure invisible again.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: I redrew the canvas as a sequencer. Left to right. Modules arranged like a signal chain — load, condition, transform, enrich, export.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The same metaphor a music producer uses to think about audio passing through effects.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The horizontal axis became the story: data starts on the left, has things done to it in the middle, ends on the right.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: There is no other path to walk. The shape of the canvas teaches the shape of the regulation.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Then the second question. If the diagram is the document, the diagram has to show risk.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Not after you click. Not after you read. At a glance. I tried colour-coded cells, heatmap overlays, badge icons — all of them turned risk into a separate vocabulary layered on top of the structure.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The DPO had to learn the dashboard before they could read it.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The Sankey clicked because it carries two dimensions in a single band.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Thickness is how much personal data is moving. Colour is how exposed that data is.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The information lives in the connection itself, not in a legend you have to consult.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A thick red band crossing a border is not a chart annotation.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: It is the picture, drawn correctly.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: That was the moment. The diagram stopped being a representation of the document and became the document.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Three principles, held together. Affordance. The canvas IS the workspace.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: You draw where you want the module to live, and the shape itself decides what it is — circle becomes Data Subject, square becomes Data Store, diamond becomes a compliance gate.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: There is no "add module" button. No mode switch. The interaction is indistinguishable from sketching on a whiteboard, except the whiteboard understands what you drew.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Transparency. The scoring model is published mathematics, not a black box.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A separate audit page imports the same code the application runs and exposes every weight, every threshold, every multiplier — with an interactive calculator that lets any regulator, auditor, or DPO verify the result themselves.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Trust is structural here, not promised.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Sovereignty. The data a ROPA tool sees is the most sensitive map in an organisation.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: AutoFlow runs entirely client-side. No server, no account, no telemetry.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The classifier runs on the device. The scoring runs on the device.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The flow never leaves the browser tab that drew it. The tool practices what the regulation preaches.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The Sankey carries two dimensions in one band. Each personal data field adds 4 pixels of band width — a connection carrying name and email is thin, a connection carrying twelve fields is visibly heavier.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The colour is computed from three factors: sensitivity (Article 9 special categories score highest), state (clear text exposes fully, encryption neutralises, anonymisation eliminates), and destination (US jurisdiction under CLOUD Act, EU encrypted access-controlled, and everything between).

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Multiply the three. Above the high threshold — red. Above the medium — orange.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Below — blue. Three colours, matching the decision space a DPO actually operates in: act now, review, or accept.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The band is a gradient, not a single colour. Source colour on the left, arrival colour on the right.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A band that leaves blue and arrives red is telling you: this data was protected when it departed, but the destination undid that protection.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A band that stays red end to end is telling you: this data was never protected at all.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The gradient is the narrative. The thickness is the scale. Together they answer "how bad is this?

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: " faster than any dashboard.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The classifier is not allowed to guess. Below the confidence threshold, the drawn strokes flash red and erase themselves.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The canvas returns to blank. A compliance tool that misinterprets a gesture produces a record that misleads the regulator.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A tool that admits uncertainty produces trust. Accountability over confidence — the same principle that governed Senz eight years earlier.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The training data comes from the same canvas as the inference data.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The first version of the classifier was trained on a public dataset of crowd-sourced drawings.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: It scored well on tests and failed on real fingers. The strokes a single user makes on a specific canvas do not look like crowd-sourced sketches.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: So the training set was redrawn — on the same canvas the tool uses to recognise.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The model is small because it is exact, trained where it lives, on the strokes it will actually see.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Not an engineering detail. The same design instinct as everything else in the tool: the territory and the map are made from the same material.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The scoring model publishes itself. audit. html is a standalone page that imports the same scoring code the application uses.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Every weight, every threshold, every multiplier is inspectable.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: An interactive calculator lets anyone pick any combination and see the score and colour update in real time.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A regulator or DPO opens the page and verifies: health record + clear + US store = red band.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Not an opinion. Arithmetic. The same arithmetic the tool runs every time a connection is made.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The schema is the architecture. Every module type owns a schema file: its fields, its risk logic, its output contract, its validation warnings.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The card component is a dumb renderer — it reads a schema, builds a form, displays the result.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: All domain knowledge lives in the schemas. Adding a new module type — FHIR healthcare bundle, NIS2 incident output, EHDS interoperability — is adding a schema file, not modifying core code.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The architecture scales by addition.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: No build step, no framework dependency. Vanilla JavaScript. Web components.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: No NPM supply chain. No forced upgrades. The application is the source code.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A sovereignty decision, not a minimalism preference — the tool is small enough to inspect end-to-end, and stable across the decade-scale timelines that compliance regulations actually live on.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: AutoFlow is in development. The outcome it points at is not a metric but a stance.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The deeper argument the tool makes is about who compliance tooling is for.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: If it is for auditors, a spreadsheet suffices — rows satisfy checkboxes.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: If it is for the people responsible for protecting personal data, the tool should make risk visible, not just recordable.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: A DPO should be able to glance at their screen and see the problem — a thick red band crossing a border — not discover it in a quarterly report.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: AutoFlow is a training tool as much as a compliance tool. The act of building the flow — drawing shapes, connecting them, watching bands change colour as you configure jurisdictions and encryption — teaches the regulation's logic.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The interaction IS the education. The colour IS the feedback.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The Sankey IS the understanding. A DPO who builds one flow learns more about their organisation's data posture than they would reading the spreadsheet they spent three months filling in.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The same architecture extends naturally. FHIR R4 bundles for EHDS healthcare interoperability.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Verifiable Credential issuance for eIDAS 2. 0. Audit trail artifacts for NIS2 incident reporting.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Each is a new schema file. The core does not change. The published scoring formula does not change.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The on-device boundary does not change.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The map should look like the territory. The tool that protects data should not be the tool that leaks it.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The mathematics behind a risk score belong in front of the user, not behind a vendor's confidence.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: These are not innovations. They are the obvious shape of the work, recovered after a decade of compliance tools that treated regulation as a billing surface rather than a design constraint.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: AutoFlow is one instance of that recovery. The principles transfer.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Built solo. Product direction, architecture, every design decision, and acceptance criteria were mine.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The tools below carried specific weight in the workflow.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Gemini — Market-signal research. I framed the questions, weighed returned signals against domain knowledge, and decided which findings shaped product direction.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Lumo — European regulation. EU-jurisdictional by design. I framed the compliance questions, tested returned interpretations against project constraints, and decided which guardrails to embed.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Claude Code (CLI) — Code pairing, refactor, and review. Implementation against constraints I defined.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: I owned acceptance, integration, and ship decisions.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: Claude (web) — Positioning and pressure-testing. Used to stress-test my own framing — challenging assumptions, surfacing competing perspectives, sharpening claims before they shipped.

sentences.title: AutoFlow
sentences.text: The principles that shaped the approach — accountability-over-confidence, on-device NLU, schema-driven architecture — carry forward from earlier collaboration with Sven Martinov and Olivier Gonthier on Senz at Kaiser X Labs.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: External Consultant — Systems Design & Prototyping — 2024 — engaged by Romain Menetrier, CPO/CTO of Dowgo Why: Due diligence platforms treat document management as an organisation problem.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: It isn't. Users can organise. What they cannot do is see what's missing, who needs to act, and what comes next — while juggling legal teams, auditors, and deadlines across borders.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: What: A two-week consulting engagement that redesigned the data room around a conversational layer.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: The file system stays. An agent sits beside it — greets you by name, surfaces what's missing, accepts delegation in natural language, and points the workspace at the next action.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Delivered as working code in the client's production stack, not a reference design.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Outcome: In production. The company raised €2M in funding shortly after and now processes €300K+ in active business through the platform.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: The redesigned data room is the surface where every one of those transactions begins.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Dowgo is a blockchain-based renewable energy investment platform.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Romain Menetrier, CPO/CTO, engaged me to redesign the due diligence data room — a regulated workflow where founders, legal teams, auditors, and investors coordinate around twenty-four required document types across ten categories.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Two weeks. One consultant. Working code delivered into the client's git repository in React and Shadcn — the same stack the development team uses in production.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Every due diligence platform on the market is built on the same paradigm: a data room.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Folders, files, upload buttons. The metaphor is a filing cabinet — a place to put things so other people can find them.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: The paradigm works. Users know how file systems behave. That fluency is an asset, not a constraint.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Users could organise. What they could not do was act. The file system showed them what existed.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: It did not show them what was missing, what was overdue, or who needed to provide what.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: Every action required holding the full mental model of the regulated process in your head — and no surface anywhere told you where you stood.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: The cognitive load did not live in filing documents. It lived in tracking the process around them.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: The brief, when Romain first described it, was to add AI categorisation.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: A modern solution for a modern platform. That instinct was wrong, and saying so was the first job.

sentences.title: Dowgo
sentences.text: I pushed back on the brief and asked for time before touching a screen.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: What: A handcrafted stone with a hidden NFC chip. Tap it to a phone, hear a parent's voice.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: End-to-end encrypted, stored on IPFS, decrypted only by physical possession of the object.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Why: We have dematerialised the things that carry memory — the voice, the touch, the object on the nightstand.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Co-parenting apps track schedules. Messaging tools store everything on servers that can be subpoenaed.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: None of them were designed for a three-year-old who cannot read, or for a family where distance is not chosen but imposed.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: How: Client-side AES-256-GCM encryption, IPFS for censorship-resistant storage, NFC serial number as key derivation input.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: No accounts, no server, no database of messages. The system is incapable of betraying its users — not by policy, but by architecture.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Proof: Working PWA with dual playback modes (persistent and ephemeral).

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The architecture designed for the hardest case serves every other case trivially.

sentences.text: — French proverb The proverb exists in every language because the pain exists in every culture.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Distance erodes presence. Absence, sustained long enough, becomes its own kind of loss — not the sharp grief of death, but the slow fade of connection stretched too thin.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: We have dematerialised most of what carries memory. The letters are gone.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The photo albums are in a cloud. The voice that said goodnight is a notification on a screen that was already dismissed.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: We traded physical presence for digital convenience and lost something we cannot name but feel every day.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Some distances are chosen. The parent who works across time zones, who trades bedtime stories for quarterly targets.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The sacrifice made for provision, paid in presence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Some distances are imposed. The military family whose parent serves on foreign soil, whose calls come at strange hours if they come at all.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: And some distances are stolen. The child taken across a border.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The parent left searching. The silence that authorities cannot even quantify.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Behind every uncounted case is a parent who cannot hold their child.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A child who cannot hear their parent's voice. I am personally familiar with this silence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: An entire industry looked at these families — all of them, from the business traveler to the abducted child — and offered them scheduling apps.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The first attempts were not stones. They were logbooks — heavily tech-oriented memory systems capturing text, pictures, timestamps, anchors in time.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: They failed the way most technology fails families: by assuming literacy, by demanding interaction, by feeling like documentation rather than connection.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A three-year-old cannot read a logbook. A six-year-old does not find comfort in a timestamped archive.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: These systems recorded presence. They did not deliver it.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Language, persistence, reading ability — each became a constraint that narrowed the question: which stimulus triggers not the recall of a memory, but the feeling of a reconforting presence?

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The research pointed in one direction. The human brain treats a familiar voice as a neurobiological safety cue.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A child recognizes their parent's voice from birth. By two months, that voice is encoded as a marker of safety — a familiar voice evokes the entire mental representation of a person, including visual memories and emotional context, even in the absence of a face.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Neuroscience has a clinical term for what a parent's voice does to a child's nervous system: non-pharmacological anxiolytic.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: It reduces anxiety without medication. Not image, not video, not text.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Voice carries the message, the sentiment, the emotions, and most importantly — the presence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The physiology is unambiguous. Hearing a loved one's voice triggers a measurable cortisol reduction — stress suppression — and a significant increase in oxytocin, the hormone that mediates bonding.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Text messaging produces neither. No cortisol change. No oxytocin release.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Physiologically identical to the control group. A text says "I love you.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: " A voice makes the body believe it.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A study of 1,772 participants found that voice-only communication consistently outperforms video in empathetic accuracy — the ability to correctly identify what another person is feeling.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Removing visual input forces the brain to focus entirely on paralinguistic cues: tone, inflection, rhythm.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Video calls can paradoxically increase distress in children by highlighting physical absence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The screen shows the parent's face but confirms they are not here.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Voice does not carry that contradiction. Voice accompanies. It does not remind you of what is missing.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Emotional voices are not only recognised more accurately — they are retained better over time.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: After one week, the memory trace of an emotional voice is nearly twice as strong as a neutral one.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A parent's voice saying goodnight is not just heard in the moment.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: It persists. The brain holds onto it because it matters.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A voice in the dark is a presence. A text in the dark is information.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Technology announces itself. Screens glow. Devices demand charging.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Gadgets require learning, updating, maintaining. A stone does not announce itself.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A stone on a nightstand is invisible. A stone in a pocket is unremarkable.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A stone in the hands of a child being monitored raises no suspicion.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The object needed to be convenient — something that fits in a child's pocket, something you could always have with you.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Watching children explore their surroundings, one thing always appealed to me: a cross-gender constant, older than any toy.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Children collect stones. Simple, dirty stones, cherished like the most precious discovery of the day — sometimes of a life.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: No child has ever been taught to pick up a stone. They just do.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Each Pebbble is hand-shaped from a water-based composite that solidifies on contact with air and reproduces the exact texture and feel of a river pebble — same grain, same weight, same way it warms progressively in your hand as you hold it.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The material allows shaping around water-resistant, sealed NFC tags without seams, without molding marks, without any visible sign that it holds anything at all.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: People discovering it for the first time try to see how it opens, what it contains.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: There is nothing to find. It is a stone.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A child might find it interesting at first. But the relationship with the stone changes when they realise it is coated with a fine luminescent layer that makes it glow in the dark — distinguishing it from every other pebble in their collection.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: And it changes again, permanently, when they witness it connect to a phone and hear a voice they love.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Not just another nice pebble. A magical one. Like the pebbles from Le Petit Poucet — the stones that lead him and his brothers and sisters back through the forest, back to their family, back to their loved ones.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: That is where the stone comes from.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Inside each one: an NFC chip. No battery. No screen. No moving parts.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Twelve cents of hardware that draws power only at the moment of reading, then waits again.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: It will wait for decades. Hold the stone to a phone. Hear your parent's voice.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A child does not need to understand IPFS or NFC. They need to understand: hold this to the phone, and you hear mama's voice.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: I collected reference pebbles from a river. They stand aligned in a box on my desk — guides for shape and weight.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Hand-shaping these stones has something relaxing about it, leaning towards meditation.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The constraint was finding a material clean enough — non-toxic once cured, safe for a child who will carry it everywhere.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Once solved, the process became straightforward. The complexity lives elsewhere.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: What lasts is simple. What matters should last. Design for the extreme case and the common case becomes trivial.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The extreme case: no reliable internet, active censorship, a monitored device, a child too young for interfaces, content that must survive hostile infrastructure, technology that must last years without maintenance.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Every layer solves a specific constraint: The stone is the key.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The encryption key is derived from the NFC tag's unique serial number plus a timestamp, run through PBKDF2 with 100,000 iterations.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The key doesn't exist anywhere — not on a server, not in the app, not in the stone.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: It is computed at the moment of reading from the physical object itself.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: No accounts, no passwords. Physical possession is the only authentication.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: IPFS distributes the voice. Content-addressed, decentralized.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Block one node, it routes through another. Block a domain — there is no domain to block.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A voice recorded in one country reaches a child in another regardless of what stands between them.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: No central server. The storage provider never sees plaintext.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: There is no database of messages, no server logs, no central point that can be compelled to reveal content.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The system is private by architecture, not by policy. There is no database of messages to subpoena.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: If a parent's voice can reach an abducted child — safely, secretly, persistently — then the military family on deployment, the divorced couple across distance, the grandparent recording stories are all already served.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The app itself serves two fundamentally different experiences.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The reader must be poetic — the interface disappearing to offer nothing but the presence of a warm voice.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: How do you design a screen that gets out of the way of a parent saying goodnight?

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The writer is the opposite problem: recording, managing, reusing messages, adding music.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A parent recording a bedtime story at 11 PM after a long day cannot afford to fight an interface.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Simplicity is not a trend here — it is the constraint that guarantees the system gets used at all.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: But the deeper split is not between reading and writing. It is between safety and evidence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A child with their own phone keeps the voice always available.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Cached, ready whenever loneliness arrives at 2 AM. But what about a child using a borrowed device?

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A shared tablet at a shelter? A phone belonging to someone who must not know what it accessed?

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Ephemeral mode: the audio plays once. When the app closes, nothing remains.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: No history, no cache, no evidence. The voice was heard, and then — nothing.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: This is the hardest design constraint I've worked with. Not technically.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Emotionally. The idea that a child needs to hear their parent's voice in secret, and that evidence of hearing it could make things worse.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Accounts. An account is a target. It can be discovered, subpoenaed, locked.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The stone authenticates by physical possession. Nothing else.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Cloud storage. A server is a single point of failure and a single point of compulsion.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: IPFS distributes content. No entity controls it.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Mobile app. An app in the app store can be found on the phone.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: A PWA launched from an NFC tap operates ephemerally — no installation, no icon, no evidence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The web is the delivery mechanism because the web can disappear.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: User-created passwords. A child cannot remember a password. The stone itself is the password.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Pebbble is one of three projects using the same architecture: NFC tag on a physical object triggers a web experience with zero intermediary.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Drop — bottle cap triggers water map. Utility. Vrooom — wooden car triggers playground discovery.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Play. Pebbble — stone triggers encrypted voice. Presence.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: Same pattern, different stakes. The NFC tap replaces the entire onboarding flow in all three.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: But only Pebbble carries the weight of what happens when the physical object is the last connection between a parent and a child.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: The architecture that makes Drop convenient makes Pebbble necessary.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: IPFS permanence is the feature for the humanitarian case. Once pinned, the voice persists independent of any server, company, or jurisdiction.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: But permanence has a cost. What about messages you later regret?

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: What about a child who grows up and wants the voice to stop?

sentences.text: This tension — between censorship resistance and the right to be forgotten — is unresolved.

sentences.text: I include this because most portfolios present resolved problems.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: This one isn't resolved. That's honest.

sentences.text: As a child, it took me hours of practice to learn to skip stones across water.

sentences.title: Pebbble
sentences.text: But what I loved most about it — and certainly why I still love it — is not the throw.

sentences.text: Each new framework, method, and tool they stacked on was meant to make them faster.

sentences.text: Instead, it raised the locking bar on budget approval — committing a full team of designers, researchers, and developers to build an MVP that was already outdated before launch.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: They didn't need more matter. They needed to rearrange what they had.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Organisations are closed systems of a different kind of matter.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Frameworks, components, design systems, data, business logic, flows, APIs, and the people who understand them — the latent potentials sitting inside every large company.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: None of it is missing. Most is underused, mis-combined, or defended by whichever team currently owns its shape.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Lavoisier, working on combustion in the 1780s, established a principle that dismantled alchemy: in a closed system, nothing new is created and nothing is lost.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Everything is transformed.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Senz was built on this principle. Momentum had come first — a tool we built to let non-experts contribute to Allianz's Angular atomic library.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: It failed. The learning curve was too steep, and the people it was supposed to empower could not climb it quickly enough to stay engaged.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The system was sophisticated. That was the problem.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: A few months later, in a meeting about the coming design system, a home claims expert walked to the whiteboard and started sketching a First Notification of Loss — boxes, hero, the few inputs a customer needs to report that something has gone wrong.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: She asked the builders whether their components could handle the cases and logic she was drawing.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: My mind slipped sideways, to Google Photos — how it had quietly crossed the threshold where labelling an image was the same thing as reading it.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Pixels into signal. Signal into structured matter the system could act on.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Paper and pen. The most radical and simple input on earth. The medium people reach for long before they turn to a computer, available in every office and every country, affordable at every economic tier.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: If Google could turn photos into structured matter at scale, we could turn drawings into production components the same way.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Momentum had tried to teach experts a new tool. Senz would meet them at the tool they already used.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Senz was built on three principles, held together. Affordance.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The interface mirrored the simplicity of the raw material it accepted.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: A canvas, a side toolbar, a predict button. No dashboard, no project setup.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Input arrived through whichever surface the user already had — a phone photo via the companion app, direct drawing on a touch-enabled laptop, drag-and-drop of pre-made wireframe elements, SVG or image upload.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Data arrived the same way: spreadsheet, CSV, database endpoint, one click through connectors.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Senz never contained data. It managed the flow between systems that already held it.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Assistance. The model was a translation layer, never a generative one.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The system recognised the user's intent but did not produce it.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Completed steps folded and dismissed as progress was made, clearing the canvas without erasing the path.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Real-time collaboration ran through mandate roles — admin, designer, reviewer, approver — so different experts could author different layers of the same prototype without colliding.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Transparency. The model was trained by design never to pretend.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Confidence thresholds were tuned to surface uncertainty rather than hide it — if the system did not recognise a shape, it said so.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Every decision was the user's, and therefore auditable by the user.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The stack was there to serve, not to harvest.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The companion app preprocessing pipeline. Users couldn't be asked to stage their shot.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: A phone photo of a real whiteboard, with glare, angle, and other people's notes in the background, had to be readable by the production system — no special paper, no careful framing, no instructions.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Browser-based capture wasn't technically possible at the time, so the companion app handled its own computer-vision preprocessing before the main model ever saw the image: object extraction, foreign-item removal, drop-shadow and flare filtering, perspective correction.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Affordance enforced upstream, not just in the UI.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: One predict button, not continuous recognition. The model ran on our own on-prem hardware.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Continuous prediction would have burned compute for marginal UX gain, and we refused it on ecological grounds.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The consequence reshaped the interaction: a deliberate predict action invited the user to think first, draw, and then translate.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The pause before pressing predict was a thinking space the tool preserved on purpose.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: A two-stage recognition pipeline. A wireframe is not a grid of pixels.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: It's a document with layout structure — a button is a button partly because of where it sits in the composition, not only because of how it looks.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The recognition ran in two stages to honour that: a detection model (RetinaNet) located the shapes on the page, and a classification model (LayoutLM) read each region in its spatial context, deciding what the shape was given what surrounded it.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The system understood composition, not just shapes.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Direct manipulation on the canvas, versioning for tested journeys.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The drawing was live material. Marks could be erased, redrawn, moved, scaled at any point — the canvas worked the way a sketchbook works, and adjustments happened in the drawing itself.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Versioning operated at a different layer. Once a prototype had been predicted and deployed — run against users, shown to stakeholders, tested in the wild — that version was preserved.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The user could then branch the project, redraw the canvas, and produce a new version to compare against the first.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: A/B testing was an intentional capability, not a side effect: projects could be cloned, deployed online with public or password-gated access, and evaluated side by side against real users.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Side-by-side prediction, then toggle. The first release showed the original drawing and the recognised version side by side by default.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: In testing we watched users begin to contort their sketches to help the model read them — the draw-predict-infinity-loop — and we moved side-by-side to a toggle.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Transparency, on demand. Default-visible uncertainty had become its own attention tax.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: On-device, sovereign model. No remote API calls. No third-party cloud dependency that could change its terms or lose compliance posture mid-project.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: This was a 2018 decision that most 2026 AI products still have not made.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The outcome was not a metric. It was a capacity. Senz bypassed the six-figure budget gate that had stood in front of every internal test.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: No one needed approval to test a business idea. A claims handler, an underwriter, a product manager could now assemble a working prototype from a sketch in days rather than quarters, deploy it, run it against real data, and archive it when it didn't work — without a developer in the chain, without a design sprint, without a proposal deck.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The unit of measurement shifted from the idea to the test. Failure became cheaper than the meeting held to debate it.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: One specific test proves the capacity worked. An in-house agent working on bike insurance — a single employee, not a consultant — used Senz to test an idea the company would not have generated otherwise.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The observation was plain: many urban cyclists were not ready to commit to monthly or yearly premiums, and the institutional default was to write them off.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The hypothesis was that this was the wrong gesture.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: What if, instead of turning these people away, the company offered them a near-zero-cost service — something small, useful, oriented toward preventing the risk they were not yet ready to insure against?

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Not a discount. Not a trial. A caring gesture: the business acknowledging it was about risk reduction, not only premium collection.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Senz made it testable in days. The prototype was assembled from existing customer data, infrastructure, and risk models — recombined into a service that would never have survived the budget approval required to build it conventionally.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The segment the company had previously been unable to reach began to engage — not with the product, but with the posture behind it.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Trust was the outcome. The service was only its instrument.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Technology like this will revolutionize the way we innovate and supports non-designers and non-developers on their way to build a digital product by themselves.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: — Kai Kölsch, Founder & CEO, Seedbox Ventures

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The matter is already there. The work doesn't belong where it used to.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: It stops being the specialist's — the consultant, the lab, the people with permission to conjure.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: It belongs to anyone who touches the matter. The CTO whose systems already contain latent capability.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The designer who has seen what the customers actually need. The claims expert at the whiteboard.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: These are the people who already know. Most of the time, they are waiting for permission.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Senz was one instrument for granting that permission. There will be others.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: The matter is rarely the obstacle. I led the project end-to-end at Kaiser X Labs (Allianz): product concept and design, full UX, end-to-end training dataset and labeling strategy, multi-framework reasoning, and the research-insights connectors that let us validate business models on real data.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Deployed, ran, and scaled the on-prem inference servers. Scaled the labeling studio.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Owned the FastAPI connectors across the ML and no-code surfaces.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Olivier Gonthier : Rebuilt the multimodal interface — touch, pen, drag-and-drop, upload.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Built the multi-framework code-mapping engine and the conditional business-logic builder.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Two earlier contributors shaped Senz before the core team came together.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Jakob Berhend : Design and documentation in Senz's early stage.

sentences.title: Senz
sentences.text: Kept the project's progress legible as the concept took shape.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: What: A wooden toy with an NFC chip links to a playground discovery PWA.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Children check in, earn badges, print them through the company website, color them, glue them into a handmade passport.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Every print sends a parent to the product catalog — without an ad, a popup, or a captured email.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Why: Children's apps monetize attention. Growth hacking monetizes trust.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Both extract more than they give. Vrooom inverts the model: the utility earns the visit, the visit earns the discovery, the discovery earns the next purchase — if the product deserves it.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: How: NFC as entry point, zero accounts, zero tracking, E2E encrypted WebRTC bridge to website for printing.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The product serves an immediate need with no compromise. The business grows because people come back, not because they're brought back.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Proof: 15 seconds of screen time per session. Zero data sent to any server.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The growth channel is a parent choosing to print something for their child.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: -- Role: Systems Designer & Product Strategist Key supporter: Thomas Duester — kept pushing when I was ready to move on.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Some projects survive because someone else refuses to let them die.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Stack: Vanilla JS, Three. js, Leaflet, Overpass API, Valhalla routing, Dexie.

sentences.title: Vrooom

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A child runs to the bench where her father sits. She holds up a stick — a wand, perhaps, or a sword, or something that has no name yet because she is still deciding.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: She wants him to see.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: He glances up from his phone. "That's nice, honey. " His eyes return to the screen.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: She waits. The stick lowers. She walks back to the grass, alone.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The phone is not the villain. The phone is the symptom. The villain is the exhaustion, the isolation, the impossible demands placed on parents who have no village.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The phone fills the vacuum we created.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: But what else could fill it? Children's apps are a billion-dollar industry built on a single transaction: silence purchased with screen time.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Engagement is the metric. Retention is the goal. The app succeeds when the child does not look up.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Behind this industry sits another one: growth hacking. Captured emails.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Retargeting pixels. Push notifications. Streak mechanics. Dark patterns dressed as engagement.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The business model requires the user to be brought back — because the product alone is not worth returning to.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: What if the product was worth returning to? A wooden car. Beech — closed grain, food-safe, built to outlast the child who holds it.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Inside: an NFC tag. Tap it to a parent's phone and a PWA opens — a playground discovery app that checks in at parks, earns badges, and gets out of the way.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Fifteen seconds of screen time per session. No account. No data sent anywhere.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: No push notifications. No streaks.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The app serves one need: a child wants to explore. It serves it completely, then disappears.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Brands win more from being remembered for what they leave behind than from what they took.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The toy does not need the phone. The phone needs the parent.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: This is the foundation. A product that respects its user has earned something no retargeting pixel can buy: trust.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A parent who trusts the product comes back. Not because they were reminded.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Because they chose to.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The shape descends from a childhood memory — matchbox cars with cork wheels.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Why those toys lasted was not their complexity. It was their simplicity.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: They were substrates for play, not scripts for it. No doors, no windows, no driver.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Every detail removed is a story the child gets to add.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Hand-planed from rectangular blocks — finding the right taper, grip, and weight happened physically, not in CAD.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The bottom tapers at front and back — not decoration, but function.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Push it like a friction toy and the taper lifts it slightly, prevents scratching, makes the glide smooth.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: There is a Japanese carpentry principle: build it in a way that it lasts as long as it took the tree to grow.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The first prototypes went to neighborhood kids. No instructions, no explanation.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: They connected with the object before anyone mentioned the app.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The wood, the weight, the shape. If the physical object does not stand alone — if it needs the digital to justify itself — the design has failed.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The NFC inside is an expansion, not a requirement.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The design goal for the first moment a child taps the car to a parent's phone: nothing less than magic.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Eyes shining. The thing in their hand was hiding this all along.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A product people love is a product people return to. That is not a marketing insight.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: It is a design decision. No avatar, no account, no login. The child's identity in the app is their wooden car.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The NFC tag carries a URL pointing to a car configuration — a 3D model with mapped parts, colors, and sounds.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Tap the car to the phone, and it appears on screen: a rendered wooden toy that spins, responds to touch, and revs its engine.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The 3D viewer captures a side-view snapshot that becomes the child's marker on the map.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Their car drives across the neighborhood as they walk.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: No "select a playground" step. No trip planning. The child walks.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: When they arrive — a playground, a park, a pool — they tap "I'm here.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: " Fresh GPS, nearest match within 150 metres, visit logged.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The badge system is designed to end in paper, not pixels. Playground badges — one per unique place visited Regular badges — earned after 10 visits to the same place Milestone badges — shields for 1, 5, 10, 25, 50 unique playgrounds

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: All badges are SVG line art. Intentionally uncolored. The badge page connects to the Vrooom website via end-to-end encrypted WebRTC — a single button, no account, no cloud.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The 3D car viewer doubles as a coloring-book generator — choose an angle and it renders a line-art outline ready for printing.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Print the badges. Cut along the lines. Color them in. Color the car.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Glue them into a handmade passport. The badges end in paper.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: But the path to paper passes through the Vrooom website. That visit is not accidental.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A parent standing at a printer, waiting for badge sheets, is standing inside the company's product catalog.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: No banner. No popup. No "you might also like. " They came because the app was useful.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: They stay because the products are visible. They return because their child earned new badges.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: This is led-growth without the growth hacking. No captured email.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: No retargeting pixel. No notification asking them to come back.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The utility earns the visit. The visit earns the discovery. The discovery earns the next purchase — if the product deserves it.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Every children's app monetizes attention. Vrooom monetizes the moment a parent chooses to print something for their child.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The difference is who holds the power in that transaction.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Gamification. No points, no streaks, no leaderboards. The moment you add streaks, you add anxiety.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A playground is not a competition.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Social features. No friends, no sharing, no "see where other kids are.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: " Social features shift focus from exploration to performance.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The child should discover playgrounds because they are curious, not because their friend did.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Turn-by-turn navigation. Vrooom shows walking routes when asked, but does not guide.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A child walking to a playground should look at the world, not at a screen.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Photo capture. Rejected — it puts the phone back in the child's hands at the moment they should be playing.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The check-in is the record. The badge is the memory.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Child-held device. The phone belongs to the parent. If the child holds the phone, the phone becomes the toy.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: If the parent holds the phone, the phone becomes the bridge.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Ads, emails, push notifications. The conventional growth toolkit.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Every one of them trades user trust for a short-term metric.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The product grows by being worth returning to, or it does not grow.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A shape that carries no date cannot become dated. A material that ages cannot become obsolete.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Fifty years from now, the same car will feel the same in a child's hand, will invite the same open stories, will wait for the same imagination to bring it alive.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: And perhaps, by then, it will carry something more. The passport stamps from trips that became legends.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The layers of memory pressed into an object, invisible as the NFC chip, present as the wood's weight.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The toy is not the legacy. The play is the legacy. The toy is just what holds it.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Vrooom is the third project in the physical-digital-bridge cluster: Drop — bottle cap triggers water map.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Utility. Pebbble — stone triggers encrypted voice. Presence.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Vrooom — wooden car triggers playground discovery. Play.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: But Vrooom adds something the others don't: the output is physical too.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The digital layer is sandwiched between two physical ones — a wooden car on one end, a paper passport on the other.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: And Vrooom carries a question the others don't ask. Drop proves that public infrastructure can replace proprietary APIs.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Pebbble proves that privacy can be enforced by architecture.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Vrooom demonstrates something else: a working system where the business model and the user's interest are structurally aligned — not by policy, not by promise, but by architecture.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The parent goes to the website because they want to, not because they were nudged.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: The companies that need this thinking are the ones starting to realize that the extraction model has a ceiling.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: Users leave. Regulation tightens. Brand trust erodes. The ones who figure out how to grow by giving more than they take will outlast the ones still optimizing click-through rates.

sentences.title: Vrooom
sentences.text: A car in the hand. A playground around the corner. The phone already forgotten.
